mcqs.question: A 30-year-old who recently arrived from a high-incidence country presents to his GP. Which test does NICE recommend as the initial test for latent TB?
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers Mantoux as the initial latent TB test for recent arrivals from high-incidence countries, with IGRA used if Mantoux is unavailable.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer Mantoux testing as the initial diagnostic test for latent TB infection in people who have recently arrived from a high‑incidence country who present to healthcare services. if this assessment is negative, offer them treatment for latent TB infection (see the section on managing latent TB in all age groups to the section on managing latent TB in children and young people ). If Mantoux testing is unavailable, offer an interferon‑gamma release assay. [new 2016]

mcqs.question: In a recent arrival from a high-incidence country, what Mantoux result counts as positive, according to NICE?

options.B: 5 mm or larger, regardless of BCG

mcqs.correctAnswerText: 5 mm or larger, regardless of BCG
mcqs.explanation: NICE defines a positive Mantoux in this context as 5 mm or larger, regardless of BCG history; active TB is then assessed before latent TB treatment is offered.

If the Mantoux test is positive (5 mm or larger, regardless of BCG history), assess for active TB; if this assessment is negative, offer them treatment for latent TB infection.

mcqs.question: A Mantoux test is positive in a new arrival. What is the next step before offering latent TB treatment?
mcqs.explanation: NICE says to assess for active TB after a positive test; only if that assessment is negative is latent TB treatment offered.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If the Mantoux test is positive (5 mm or larger, regardless of BCG history), assess for active TB; if this assessment is negative, offer them treatment for latent TB infection.
if this assessment is negative, offer them treatment for latent TB infection. [2011, amended 2016]

mcqs.question: Which test does NICE recommend offering before starting treatment for latent TB?
mcqs.explanation: NICE recommends offering HIV testing before starting latent TB treatment.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer testing for HIV before starting treatment for latent TB. See the NICE guidelines on increasing the uptake of HIV testing among black Africans in England and increasing the uptake of HIV testing among men who have sex with men . [new 2016]

mcqs.question: A 40-year-old is a close contact of someone with pulmonary TB. Which latent TB test does the stored NICE recommendation offer for adults aged 18–65?
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers Mantoux testing to diagnose latent TB in adults aged 18–65 who are close contacts of a person with pulmonary or laryngeal TB.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer Mantoux testing to diagnose latent TB in adults aged 18 to 65 who are close contacts of a person with pulmonary or laryngeal TB.

mcqs.question: An asymptomatic close contact of a pulmonary TB case is 72 years old. What does NICE suggest considering?

options.C: Treatment for latent TB in all contacts

mcqs.explanation: For asymptomatic close contacts older than 65, NICE suggests considering a chest X-ray, possibly leading to further investigation for active TB.

sourceRefs.excerpt: In asymptomatic close contacts older than 65 years, consider a chest X‑ray (if there are no contraindications), possibly leading to further investigation for active TB. [2006, amended 2016]

mcqs.question: A passenger on a long-haul flight is later diagnosed with TB. What does NICE advise about contact tracing of fellow passengers?

options.C: Trace the whole cabin by IGRA

mcqs.explanation: NICE advises against routinely contact tracing fellow aircraft passengers after a TB diagnosis in a traveller.

sourceRefs.excerpt: After diagnosis of TB in an aircraft traveller, do not routinely carry out contact tracing of fellow passengers. [2006, amended 2016]

mcqs.question: A physician diagnoses active TB. When does NICE say contact tracing should start?

options.A: Only after culture confirmation is back
options.C: Only after formal notification is made
options.E: After 2 weeks of the patient's treatment

mcqs.explanation: NICE says the diagnosing physician should inform colleagues so contact tracing can be assessed without delay; it should not wait for notification.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Once a person has been diagnosed with active TB, the diagnosing physician should inform relevant colleagues so that the need for contact tracing can be assessed without delay. Contact tracing should not be delayed until notification. [2006]

mcqs.question: Which group of contacts does NICE advise NOT to assess routinely?

options.A: All household contacts of the case
options.B: Social contacts, including most at work
options.C: Neonates in close contact with the case
options.D: Contacts of children with active TB
options.E: Close contacts of laryngeal TB cases

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Social contacts, including most at work
mcqs.explanation: NICE advises against routinely assessing social contacts of people with TB, which includes most workplace contacts.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not routinely assess social contacts of people with TB, who will include most workplace contacts. [2006, amended 2016]

mcqs.question: A child is diagnosed with pulmonary TB. What does NICE recommend about contact investigation?

options.A: No contact tracing is needed for children
options.B: Investigate contacts to find the source
options.C: Screen only the child's school classmates
options.D: Wait for the child's own culture result
options.E: Test only the child's brothers and sisters

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Investigate contacts to find the source
mcqs.explanation: NICE recommends investigating everyone in contact with children who have TB, looking beyond close contacts if needed, to find the primary source of infection.

sourceRefs.excerpt: In all types of contact investigation scenarios (active case finding, incident or outbreak investigations) multidisciplinary TB teams should investigate all people who have been in contact with children who have pulmonary or extrapulmonary TB to identify the primary source of infection. If necessary, they should look beyond immediate close contacts to find the source. [2012, amended 2016]

mcqs.question: A neonate has been in close contact with someone with smear-positive pulmonary TB who has had less than 2 weeks of treatment. After assessing for active TB, what does NICE recommend starting?
mcqs.explanation: For this situation, NICE recommends assessing for active TB and starting isoniazid with pyridoxine.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If a neonate has been in close contact with people with smear‑positive pulmonary or laryngeal TB who have not had at least 2 weeks of anti‑TB treatment: Assess for active TB (see the sections on diagnosing active TB in all age groups , diagnosing pulmonary (including laryngeal) TB in all age groups and diagnosing pulmonary (including laryngeal) TB in children and young people ). Start isoniazid (with pyridoxine). Carry out a Mantoux test after 6 weeks of treatment. If the Mantoux test is inconcl

mcqs.question: A Mantoux-negative 28-year-old, previously unvaccinated, is a contact of pulmonary TB. What does NICE offer?
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers BCG to Mantoux-negative, previously unvaccinated contacts of pulmonary or laryngeal TB aged 35 or younger, or older healthcare and laboratory workers.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer BCG vaccination to Mantoux‑negative contacts of people with pulmonary and laryngeal TB (see the section on diagnosing latent TB in all age groups ) if they: have not been vaccinated previously (that is, there is no adequate documentation or a BCG scar) and are aged 35 years or younger or are aged 36 years and older and a healthcare or laboratory worker who has contact with patients or clinical materials. [2006, amended 2016]

mcqs.question: A new NHS employee from a low-incidence country, with no BCG, will have patient contact. Their Mantoux test is positive. What does NICE recommend next?
mcqs.explanation: For such employees NICE recommends offering an IGRA if the Mantoux is positive; if the IGRA is positive, assess for active TB.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer a Mantoux test to new NHS employees who will be in contact with patients or clinical materials, if the employees: are not new entrants from high‑incidence countries and have not had BCG vaccination (for example, they are without a BCG scar, other documentation or a reliable history). If the Mantoux test is positive, offer an interferon‑gamma release assay. If this is positive, assess for active TB; if this assessment is negative, offer them treatment for latent TB infection. [2011, amended

mcqs.question: Which group does NICE say should be screened for TB to the same standard as new healthcare employees?

options.A: Visitors to clinical areas and inpatient wards
options.B: Patients' relatives staying with them overnight
options.C: Office staff with no patient contact at all

mcqs.explanation: NICE says clinical students, agency and locum staff and contract ancillary workers with patient contact should be screened to the same standard as new employees.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Screen clinical students, agency and locum staff and contract ancillary workers who have contact with patients or clinical materials for TB to the same standard as new employees in healthcare environments, according to the recommendations set out above. Seek documentary evidence of screening to this standard from locum agencies and contractors who carry out their own screening. [2006]

mcqs.question: A patient with suspected active TB is referred urgently to the TB clinic. Which results does NICE want available before the specialist review?
mcqs.explanation: NICE asks for first-line tests, including sputum smear and chest X-ray, to be available before the specialist review, without delaying the referral.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Healthcare professionals should consider urgent referral to TB clinics for people with suspected active TB. They should also ensure the results from first‑line diagnostic tests (including a sputum smear and chest X‑ray) are available before the person sees a specialist. (Note: this should not delay the referral.) [2012, amended 2016]

mcqs.question: A patient with suspected TB needs urgent treatment before sensitivity results are back, and there is concern about drug resistance. What does NICE suggest?

options.A: Manage as MDR-TB until results return
options.C: Withhold all treatment until results return
options.D: Treat for latent TB only, pending results
options.E: Give BCG and review when results return

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Manage as MDR-TB until results return
mcqs.explanation: If urgent treatment is needed, NICE suggests considering managing as multidrug-resistant TB until sensitivity results are available.

sourceRefs.excerpt: if urgent treatment is needed, consider managing as multidrug‑resistant TB until sensitivity results are available. [new 2016]

mcqs.question: What does NICE recommend offering every person with TB to identify their needs?

options.A: A risk assessment for enhanced case management
options.B: Admission to a negative-pressure isolation room
options.C: Routine bronchoscopy to confirm the diagnosis
options.E: Monthly CT chest scans throughout treatment

mcqs.correctAnswerText: A risk assessment for enhanced case management
mcqs.explanation: NICE recommends a risk assessment for every person with TB to identify needs, including whether enhanced case management with directly observed therapy is required.

sourceRefs.excerpt: offer a risk assessment to every person with TB, to identify their needs and whether they should have enhanced case management including directly observed therapy

mcqs.question: Within what time should prison health staff report suspected or confirmed TB to the local TB team, according to NICE?
mcqs.explanation: NICE asks prison and immigration removal centre staff to report all suspected and confirmed TB cases to the TB team within 1 working day; TB staff should visit within 5 working days.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Prison and immigration removal centre health staff should report all suspected and confirmed TB cases to the local multidisciplinary TB team within 1 working day. [2012]
Multidisciplinary TB staff should visit every confirmed TB case in a prison or immigration removal centre in their locality within 5 working days. [2012]

mcqs.question: Which strategies does NICE suggest for helping people complete TB treatment?

options.A: Avoiding written information to reduce worry
options.B: Stopping treatment after the first month
options.D: Fines or sanctions for any missed doses
options.E: Hospital admission for the whole course

mcqs.explanation: NICE suggests reminder letters, calls, texts and apps, health education counselling and tailored support to encourage adherence and prevent early stopping.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Multidisciplinary TB teams should implement strategies for active and latent TB to encourage people to follow the treatment plan and prevent people stopping treatment early. mcqs.question: What does the stored USPSTF 2023 recommendation say about latent TB infection?
mcqs.explanation: The stored USPSTF 2023 statement says that screening for latent TB infection is recommended in adults.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Screening for latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) is recommended in adults.

mcqs.question: A 45-year-old has a differentiated thyroid cancer staged T3 with N1 nodal disease. What surgery does NICE recommend?
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers total thyroidectomy for T3/T4 tumours, N1 disease, adverse pathology or distant metastases.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer total thyroidectomy to people who have: a T3 or T4 stage primary tumour; regional lymph node involvement (N1); adverse pathological features; distant metastatic disease (M1).

mcqs.question: A 2 cm differentiated thyroid tumour (T1b N0 M0) is diagnosed. Which surgical options does NICE offer?
mcqs.explanation: For differentiated tumours larger than 1 cm or multifocal disease up to T2N0M0, NICE offers hemithyroidectomy or total thyroidectomy.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer hemithyroidectomy or total thyroidectomy to people with: differentiated thyroid tumours larger than 1 cm or multifocal disease ( T1a [m] to T2N0M0 ).

mcqs.question: After hemithyroidectomy, histology shows features that warrant further surgery. What does NICE recommend?
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers completion thyroidectomy after hemithyroidectomy when review of the initial specimen's histology indicates it.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer completion thyroidectomy to people who have had a hemithyroidectomy if it is indicated on review of the histological features of the initial specimen.

mcqs.question: After total thyroidectomy and RAI for differentiated thyroid cancer, what TSH target does NICE set for thyroid hormone suppression?
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers thyroid hormone at doses that suppress TSH to below 0.1 mIU/litre after total or completion thyroidectomy and RAI.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer thyroid hormone at doses that will suppress TSH to below 0.1 mIU/litre to people who have had total or completion thyroidectomy and RAI.

mcqs.question: How often does NICE recommend thyroglobulin monitoring in the first 2 years after RAI ablation?
mcqs.explanation: NICE recommends measuring thyroglobulin with thyroglobulin antibodies every 3–6 months for the first 2 years after RAI, then every 6–12 months.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer thyroglobulin measurement alongside measurement of thyroglobulin antibodies for people with differentiated thyroid cancer who have had total or completion thyroidectomy and RAI . Measure at: 3- to 6-month intervals in the first 2 years after RAI ablation and 6- to 12-month intervals thereafter.

mcqs.question: Why does NICE recommend measuring thyroglobulin antibodies alongside thyroglobulin?

options.A: They guide the dose of levothyroxine
options.C: They replace the need for neck imaging
options.D: They are paired in follow-up after RAI
options.E: They are used to diagnose Graves' disease

mcqs.correctAnswerText: They are paired in follow-up after RAI
mcqs.explanation: NICE specifies thyroglobulin measured together with thyroglobulin antibodies for follow-up after total or completion thyroidectomy and RAI.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer thyroglobulin measurement alongside measurement of thyroglobulin antibodies for people with differentiated thyroid cancer who have had total or completion thyroidectomy and RAI . Measure at: 3- to 6-month intervals in the first 2 years after RAI ablation and 6- to 12-month intervals thereafter.

mcqs.question: A patient has had a solitary T1a microcarcinoma completely removed. What does NICE advise about follow-up?
mcqs.explanation: NICE advises not routinely following up people with a surgically removed solitary microcarcinoma (T1a).

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not routinely follow up people with thyroid cancer who have a solitary microcarcinoma ( T1a ) that has been surgically removed.

mcqs.question: Which agent does NICE recommend for pretherapeutic stimulation before RAI ablation?
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers thyrotropin alfa for pretherapeutic stimulation before RAI ablation, including in distant metastatic disease (off-label in December 2022).

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer thyrotropin alfa for pretherapeutic stimulation for people with thyroid cancer (including those with distant metastases; see recommendation 1.3.13) who are having RAI ablation. In December 2022 this use of thyrotropin alfa as a treatment for thyroid cancer for people with distant metastases was off-label. See NICE's information on prescribing medicines .

mcqs.question: A patient has T2 disease after total thyroidectomy, with none of the features that mandate total thyroidectomy. What does NICE suggest about RAI?
mcqs.explanation: For T2 disease without the high-risk features, NICE suggests considering RAI rather than offering it routinely.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider RAI for people with T2 disease who have had a total or completion thyroidectomy, but whose cancer does not show any of the features in the recommendations on offering total thyroidectomy in the section on surgery and active surveillance for primary tumours .

mcqs.question: Which phrase does NICE advise clinicians to avoid when talking to patients about thyroid cancer?
mcqs.explanation: NICE advises against calling thyroid cancer a 'good cancer', because many people don't find it reassuring and it can make their diagnosis feel unimportant.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not refer to thyroid cancer as a 'good cancer' because many people do not find this reassuring and it can cause them to feel that their diagnosis is unimportant.

mcqs.question: What is the stated aim of RAI in the NICE patient information recommendation?

options.A: Shrink the goitre before planned surgery
options.D: Destroy residual tissue and aid monitoring

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Destroy residual tissue and aid monitoring
mcqs.explanation: NICE explains that RAI aims to destroy residual thyroid tissue, including any malignant tissue, and allows recurrence to be monitored with a blood test.

mcqs.question: A 38-year-old has Graves' disease with no compression, suspected malignancy, pregnancy plans or active eye disease, and antithyroid drugs are unlikely to give remission. What is NICE's first-line definitive treatment?
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers RAI as first-line definitive treatment for Graves' disease unless antithyroid drugs are likely to achieve remission or RAI is unsuitable.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer radioactive iodine as first-line definitive treatment for adults with Graves' disease, unless antithyroid drugs are likely to achieve remission (see recommendation 1.6.11), or it is unsuitable (for example, there are concerns about compression, malignancy is suspected, they are pregnant or trying to become pregnant or father a child within the next 4 to 6 months, or they have active thyroid eye disease). Follow the 2017 regulations on medical exposure to ionising radiation .

mcqs.question: A woman with Graves' disease plans to become pregnant within 4 months. Which treatment does NICE list as unsuitable?
mcqs.explanation: NICE lists pregnancy, or planning pregnancy or fathering a child within 4–6 months, as making RAI unsuitable.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer radioactive iodine as first-line definitive treatment for adults with Graves' disease, unless antithyroid drugs are likely to achieve remission (see recommendation 1.6.11), or it is unsuitable (for example, there are concerns about compression, malignancy is suspected, they are pregnant or trying to become pregnant or father a child within the next 4 to 6 months, or they have active thyroid eye disease). Follow the 2017 regulations on medical exposure to ionising radiation .

mcqs.question: When does NICE offer total thyroidectomy first-line for Graves' disease?

options.A: Any patient under 40 years with Graves' disease
options.B: Compression, suspected cancer, or RAI/ATD unsuitable
options.C: All relapses within 3 months of stopping drugs
options.D: Patients who would rather avoid taking any tablets daily
options.E: All patients with a visible goitre at diagnosis

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Compression, suspected cancer, or RAI/ATD unsuitable
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers total thyroidectomy first-line in Graves' disease if there are concerns about compression, suspected malignancy, or RAI and antithyroid drugs are unsuitable.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer total thyroidectomy as first-line definitive treatment for adults with Graves' disease if: there are concerns about compression, or thyroid malignancy is suspected, or radioactive iodine and antithyroid drugs are unsuitable.

mcqs.question: If RAI and surgery are unsuitable in adult Graves' disease, what antithyroid drug course does NICE offer?
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers a 12–18 month course of antithyroid drugs as first-line definitive treatment when RAI and surgery are unsuitable.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer antithyroid drugs (a 12- to 18-month course) as first-line definitive treatment for adults with Graves' disease if radioactive iodine and surgery are unsuitable.

mcqs.question: An adult has hyperthyroidism from a single toxic nodule. What first-line definitive treatment does NICE offer?
mcqs.explanation: For a single toxic nodule, NICE offers RAI (if suitable) or hemithyroidectomy, with lifelong antithyroid drugs if neither is suitable.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer radioactive iodine (if suitable) or surgery (hemithyroidectomy) as first-line definitive treatment for adults with hyperthyroidism secondary to a single nodule, or life-long antithyroid drugs if these options are unsuitable.

mcqs.question: What does the stored NCCN 2015 recommendation say about advanced or metastatic anaplastic thyroid cancer?

options.B: Observation is preferred to any therapy

mcqs.explanation: NCCN 2015 states that single-agent cisplatin is not recommended for advanced or metastatic anaplastic thyroid cancer.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Single-agent cisplatin is not recommended for patients with advanced or metastatic anaplastic thyroid cancer.

mcqs.question: A patient has a rapidly growing, stony-hard neck mass. What does the ENDOCAN TUTHYREF 2025 consensus advise?
mcqs.explanation: With clinical suspicion of anaplastic thyroid cancer, the consensus advises urgent diagnostic work-up so treatment can start promptly.

sourceRefs.excerpt: In cases of clinical suspicion of anaplastic thyroid cancer (rapid growth, stony neck mass), diagnostic work-up should be carried out urgently to enable prompt treatment.

mcqs.question: A 2007 trial in DTC patients prepared with rhTSH compared ablation activities. What did it conclude?

options.E: 1850 MBq was as effective as 3700 MBq

mcqs.correctAnswerText: 1850 MBq was as effective as 3700 MBq
mcqs.explanation: The stored abstract reports that 1850 MBq of 131I was as effective as 3700 MBq for ablation in rhTSH-prepared DTC patients, even with node metastases.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Similar rates of ablation were obtained in both groups also in patients with node metastases. Conclusion Therapeutic (131)I activities of 1850 MBq are equally effective as 3700 MBq for thyroid ablation in DTC patients prepared with rhTSH, even in the presence of node metastases.

mcqs.question: Thyroid cancer is diagnosed in pregnancy and surgery is needed. Which trimester does the stored Spanish 2014 guidance advise?
mcqs.explanation: The SEEN 2014 guidance advises performing surgery for differentiated thyroid cancer in the second trimester if it is needed during pregnancy.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: Sociedad Española de Endocrinología y Nutrición
sourceRefs.excerpt: If surgery for differentiated thyroid cancer is needed during pregnancy, it should be performed during the second trimester.

mcqs.question: An older adult reports faecal incontinence. What does NICE say should happen before any treatment is considered?
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers a focused baseline assessment to identify contributing factors before any treatment, followed by appropriate initial management.

mcqs.question: Which assessment pitfall does NICE warn about specifically in faecal incontinence?
mcqs.explanation: NICE describes faecal incontinence as a symptom with multiple contributing factors and warns against assuming a single primary cause ('diagnostic overshadowing').

sourceRefs.excerpt: When assessing faecal incontinence healthcare professionals should: be aware that faecal incontinence is a symptom, often with multiple contributory factors for an individual; avoid making simplistic assumptions that causation is related to a single primary diagnosis ('diagnostic overshadowing').

options.A: Urinary retention and pelvic organ prolapse
options.B: Faecal loading, diarrhoea, cancer red flags

options.E: Obesity, smoking and excess alcohol use

options.A: A high-fibre diet and fluids alone

options.C: Anal plugs worn during the day

mcqs.question: Faecal incontinence continues after specialised conservative management. Which investigation does NICE list first for specialist assessment?
mcqs.explanation: NICE lists anorectal physiology studies and endoanal ultrasound, with MRI or other ultrasound if endoanal ultrasound is unavailable, plus proctography as indicated.

sourceRefs.excerpt: People with continuing faecal incontinence after specialised conservative management should be considered for specialist assessment, including: anorectal physiology studies; endoanal ultrasound; if this is not available, magnetic resonance imaging, endovaginal ultrasound and perineal ultrasound should be considered; other tests, including proctography, as indicated.

mcqs.question: If endoanal ultrasound is unavailable for specialist assessment, which alternative does NICE suggest?
mcqs.explanation: NICE suggests considering MRI, endovaginal ultrasound or perineal ultrasound when endoanal ultrasound isn't available.

sourceRefs.excerpt: People with continuing faecal incontinence after specialised conservative management should be considered for specialist assessment, including: anorectal physiology studies; endoanal ultrasound; if this is not available, magnetic resonance imaging, endovaginal ultrasound and perineal ultrasound should be considered; other tests, including proctography, as indicated.

mcqs.question: A trial of sacral nerve stimulation fails. What does NICE say may be considered next?
mcqs.explanation: After an unsuccessful sacral nerve stimulation trial, a neosphincter (stimulated graciloplasty or artificial anal sphincter) can be considered.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If a trial of sacral nerve stimulation is unsuccessful, an individual can be considered for a neosphincter, for which the 2 options are a stimulated graciloplasty or an artificial anal sphincter. See also the NICE interventional procedures guidance on stimulated graciloplasty for faecal incontinence . People should be informed of the potential benefits and limitations of both procedures. Those offered these procedures should be informed that they may experience evacuatory disorders and/or seriou

mcqs.question: When does NICE say a stoma should be considered for faecal incontinence?

options.B: As first-line treatment in older patients
options.C: After a failed trial of loperamide
options.D: After other options are all considered
options.E: Only in people with spinal cord injury

mcqs.correctAnswerText: After other options are all considered
mcqs.explanation: A stoma is considered only once all appropriate non-surgical and surgical options, including those at specialist centres, have been considered.

sourceRefs.excerpt: A stoma should be considered for people with faecal incontinence that severely restricts lifestyle only once all appropriate non-surgical and surgical options, including those at specialist centres, have been considered. Individuals should be informed of the potential benefits, risks and long-term effects of this procedure. Individuals assessed as possible candidates for a stoma should be referred to a stoma care service.

mcqs.question: How does NICE advise supplying disposable pads for faecal incontinence?
mcqs.explanation: NICE states pads should be supplied in quantities sufficient for the person's needs and that limiting the number is inappropriate.

sourceRefs.excerpt: People with faecal incontinence should be offered: disposable body-worn pads in a choice of styles and designs and disposable bed pads if needed; pads in quantities sufficient for the individual's continence needs – it is inappropriate to limit the number of pads given; anal plugs (for people who can tolerate them); skin-care advice that covers both cleansing and barrier products; advice on odour control and laundry needs; disposable gloves.

mcqs.question: In which settings does NICE suggest considering a faecal collection device?
mcqs.explanation: NICE suggests considering faecal collection devices for patients in intensive care or palliative care with faecal incontinence and loose stools.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Healthcare professionals should consider a faecal collection device for people in intensive care settings and people receiving palliative care with faecal incontinence and associated loose stools.

mcqs.question: When reviewing medicines in faecal incontinence, what does NICE recommend?

options.C: Stop all regular medicines straight away
options.D: Add regular laxatives for every patient

mcqs.explanation: NICE recommends considering alternatives to drugs that may be contributing to faecal incontinence.

sourceRefs.excerpt: When reviewing medication, healthcare professionals should consider alternatives to drugs that might be contributing to faecal incontinence. (see table 4 )

mcqs.question: A person with severe cognitive impairment has incontinence that persists after initial management. What does NICE recommend?

options.B: Anal plugs as the sole management
options.E: Restraint near the toilet when needed

mcqs.explanation: NICE refers such patients for behavioural and functional analysis, followed by cause-specific interventions based on structured goal planning.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If baseline assessment and initial management have failed to resolve faecal incontinence, people with confirmed severe cognitive impairment should be referred for a behavioural and functional analysis to determine if there is any behavioural reason for faecal incontinence. Following analysis, people should be offered cause-specific interventions founded on structured goal planning that aim to resolve as well as manage behavioural aspects that may be contributing to faecal incontinence. In cases

mcqs.question: Because faecal incontinence is stigmatising, how does NICE advise approaching high-risk groups?
mcqs.explanation: NICE advises healthcare professionals to actively yet sensitively ask high-risk groups about symptoms.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Because faecal incontinence is a socially stigmatising condition, healthcare professionals should actively yet sensitively enquire about symptoms in high-risk groups (see box 1).

mcqs.question: A 2015 randomised trial compared percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS) with something it had not previously been tested against. What was the comparator?
mcqs.explanation: The stored abstract notes PTNS had shown benefit in case series (50–80%) but had not been tested against sham stimulation, which the trial set out to do.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Background Percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS) is a new ambulatory therapy for faecal incontinence. Data from case series suggest it has beneficial outcomes in 50-80% patients; however its effectiveness against sham electrical stimulation has not been investigated. We therefore aime

mcqs.question: Which supporting measures did the International Consultation on Incontinence (2010) back by expert opinion?
mcqs.explanation: ICI 2010 supports general health education, teaching about bowel function and lifestyle advice for adults with faecal incontinence (expert opinion).

sourceRefs.excerpt: General health education, patient teaching about bowel function, and advice on lifestyle modification are supported by expert opinion for the management of faecal incontinence in adults.

mcqs.question: NICE suggests screening people with faecal incontinence for which additional problem?
mcqs.explanation: NICE recommends considering screening for malnutrition or its risk, with reference to its nutrition support guideline.

sourceRefs.excerpt: consider the opportunity to screen people with faecal incontinence for malnutrition, or risk of malnutrition. See the NICE guideline on nutrition support for adults .

mcqs.question: A person with neurological or spinal injury and some residual motor function remains symptomatic after initial management. What does NICE suggest?
mcqs.explanation: NICE asks clinicians to consider whether these patients could benefit from specialised management.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Healthcare professionals should consider in particular whether people with neurological or spinal disease/injury resulting in faecal incontinence, who have some residual motor function and are still symptomatic after baseline assessment and initial management, could benefit from specialised management (see also section 1.7 ).
