topics.topicDisplayName: Early mobilization and physical rehabilitation in ICU
topics.coverageNote: WARNING: the pool has no ICU-specific trial or guideline rows. It consists entirely of NICE rehabilitation recommendations (trauma rehab NG211, stroke NG236 with 2013/2023 tags, MSCC 2023) with no stored sourceYear, so it can't be dated and isn't marked outdated. Questions test general rehabilitation principles, not ICU mobilisation evidence. Key missing source: NICE CG83/QS158 rehabilitation after critical illness, or ICU mobilisation RCTs.

mcqs.question: What does NICE say about timing acute treatment in relation to rehabilitation after traumatic injury?

options.B: Avoid delays so rehabilitation can start early
options.C: Complete all surgery first, whatever the delay

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Avoid delays so rehabilitation can start early
mcqs.explanation: NICE advises avoiding delays in acute treatment so rehabilitation can start as soon as possible, for example to maintain movement.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Avoid delays in acute treatment so that rehabilitation can start as soon as possible, for example, to maintain movement.

mcqs.question: When does NICE recommend starting a tailored exercise programme after traumatic injury?

options.A: Only once full weight-bearing is allowed
options.B: As soon as possible, at any age or stage
options.C: After 3 months, once healing is complete
options.D: Only in people younger than 65 years
options.E: Only after the person is discharged home

mcqs.correctAnswerText: As soon as possible, at any age or stage
mcqs.explanation: A tailored exercise programme should start as soon as possible, irrespective of age, stage of rehabilitation or combination of injuries.

sourceRefs.excerpt: As soon as possible after a traumatic injury, start a tailored exercise programme to help with reconditioning, fitness, strengthening, balance, proprioception and vestibular function, irrespective of the person's age, stage of rehabilitation or combination of injuries. The exercise programme: could be self-directed and/or delivered as one-to-one sessions or in a group; should include resistance training, core strengthening exercises and general aerobic fitness; should include task-specific balan

mcqs.question: After limb reconstruction, when does NICE recommend starting rehabilitation therapy?
mcqs.explanation: Rehabilitation should start as early as possible after limb reconstruction, ideally the day after surgery, to maintain range of movement.

sourceRefs.excerpt: After limb reconstruction, start rehabilitation therapy as early as possible (ideally the day after surgery) to maintain range of movement. This may include: splinting; exercise; pain management; swelling and oedema management; hand therapy; mobility; positioning.

mcqs.question: A patient has had an amputation and the prosthesis isn't ready yet. What does NICE advise?
mcqs.explanation: NICE says not to wait for prosthetics to be fitted before starting rehabilitation after limb loss.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not wait for prosthetics to be fitted before starting rehabilitation after limb loss or amputation.

mcqs.question: Which validated tool, listed by NICE for rehabilitation needs assessment, is specifically for post-ICU patients?
mcqs.explanation: NICE lists the rehabilitation complexity scale, PCAT, the complex needs checklist and the post-ICU presentation screen (PICUPS).

sourceRefs.excerpt: Use validated tools (for example, the rehabilitation complexity scale [RCS], patient categorisation tool [PCAT], complex needs checklist [CNC] or post-ICU presentation screen [PICUPS]), in the rehabilitation needs assessment to determine the need for early referral to specialist rehabilitation units.

mcqs.question: What does NICE suggest about how often rehabilitation therapies are scheduled?

options.B: Daily, with no rest days at all

mcqs.explanation: NICE suggests delivering therapy with regular breaks (for example weekdays only) to allow rest and time to review progress.

sourceRefs.excerpt: consider delivering rehabilitation therapies with regular breaks (for example, only during weekdays to allow for rest periods at weekends and time to review progress)

mcqs.question: According to NICE, what should happen to the start time and intensity of a rehabilitation programme?
mcqs.explanation: Start time, frequency, intensity and duration should be tailored. A short intensive burst at a key time may beat long weekly sessions.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Tailor the start time, frequency, intensity and duration of the rehabilitation programme to have the most beneficial effect on the person's recovery (for example, a short period of intensive rehabilitation at an important time point might be better than weekly sessions over a long period).

mcqs.question: Which interventions does NICE suggest to help early sitting after spinal cord injury?
mcqs.explanation: NICE suggests progressive sitting and tilt-table work to increase mobility and help early sitting after spinal cord injury.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider interventions (for example, progressive sitting, tilt table) to increase mobility and aid early sitting as soon as possible after a spinal cord injury.

mcqs.question: Which upper limb rehabilitation intervention after stroke does NICE advise against?
mcqs.explanation: NICE advises against offering robot-assisted arm training as part of upper limb rehabilitation.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not offer robot-assisted arm training as part of an upper limb rehabilitation programme. [2023]

mcqs.question: A stroke patient can't manage 3 hours of therapy a day. What does NICE still require?

options.D: Therapy at least 5 days a week

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Therapy at least 5 days a week
mcqs.explanation: Any therapy needed should still be offered at least 5 days a week.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Where it is agreed with the person after stroke that they are unable, or do not wish, to participate in rehabilitation therapy for at least 3 hours a day, on at least 5 days of the week, ensure that any therapy needed is still offered for a minimum of 5 days per week. [2023]

mcqs.question: Which stroke patients does NICE offer early supported discharge?

options.A: Only those who live without carers
options.E: Those who can transfer bed to chair

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Those who can transfer bed to chair
mcqs.explanation: Early supported discharge is for people who can move from bed to chair independently or with help, if a safe home environment can be provided.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer early supported discharge to people after stroke who can move from a bed to a chair independently or with assistance, as long as a safe and secure environment can be provided. [2013]

mcqs.question: When does NICE suggest a trial of electrical stimulation after stroke?

options.A: Contraction, but can't move against resistance
options.B: Full strength has already been recovered
options.C: No muscle activity at all in the affected arm
options.D: Only for leg weakness, not the upper limb
options.E: Only in the first 24 hours after the stroke

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Contraction, but can't move against resistance
mcqs.explanation: NICE considers electrical stimulation when there is muscle contraction but the arm can't move against resistance.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider a trial of electrical stimulation therapy as part of a comprehensive rehabilitation programme for people who have evidence of muscle contraction after stroke but cannot move their arm against resistance. [2013]

mcqs.question: Which outcome tools does NICE recommend for monitoring rehabilitation progress in adults?
mcqs.explanation: NICE recommends patient-reported (PROMs) and clinician-reported (CROMs) outcome measures.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Monitor the person's progress after starting rehabilitation. Use tools such as patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and clinician-reported outcome measures (CROMs) for adults; parent- and child-reported measures for children and young people; and consider using tools that involve family members and carers. Additional specific clinical assessments may be used as appropriate.

mcqs.question: What does NICE suggest about follow-up after discharge from rehabilitation?

options.D: A written leaflet at discharge only

mcqs.explanation: NICE suggests ongoing contact with education and structured review, which could be by telephone or video.

sourceRefs.excerpt: After hospital discharge, consider ongoing contact between the rehabilitation team and the person, and their family members and carers (as appropriate), with education and a structured review of progress in rehabilitation as part of outpatient follow-up. This could be offered by telephone or video link.

mcqs.question: What example of an intensive rehabilitation programme does NICE give for commissioners?
mcqs.explanation: NICE suggests commissioning intensive programmes, for example 3 weeks, residential or outpatient.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider commissioning intensive (for example, 3‑week) residential or outpatient rehabilitation programmes for people of all ages in addition to existing rehabilitation pathways, for example, as a tertiary service for trauma rehabilitation within the trauma network.

mcqs.question: Which measures does NICE list to optimise a patient's ability to engage in the rehabilitation needs assessment?
mcqs.explanation: Measures include pain management, resolving infections and resolving acute confusion or delirium.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The multidisciplinary team should assess the person's rehabilitation needs as soon as possible after the traumatic injury, when measures are being taken to optimise their ability to engage in the assessment process. These measures include: pain management; resolution of infections; resolution of acute confusion or delirium; consideration of psychological wellbeing; making available hearing aids, glasses, dentures and other orthodontic appliances; access to communication aids (if needed); access

mcqs.question: How often should a rehabilitation MDT member discuss the patient after traumatic injury, according to NICE?

options.B: Only if the patient requests it
options.D: Only at the point of discharge

mcqs.explanation: A rehabilitation MDT member should discuss the patient's rehabilitation at daily trauma meetings or ward rounds.

sourceRefs.excerpt: A member of the rehabilitation multidisciplinary team should discuss the person's rehabilitation at daily trauma meetings or ward rounds.

mcqs.question: What does NICE suggest to keep aerobic fitness during rehabilitation after injury?
mcqs.explanation: NICE suggests considering a continued programme of aerobic exercise at appropriate points along the pathway.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider a continued programme of aerobic exercise when agreeing a rehabilitation plan and at appropriate points along the rehabilitation pathway.

mcqs.question: Which principle underpins the NICE rehabilitation plan?

options.B: Kept from the patient to avoid anxiety
options.D: Written by one clinician working alone

mcqs.explanation: The plan should be personalised to the person's agreed goals, developed with them and the MDT, in clear English, as a single document.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The rehabilitation plan should be: a tailored and personalised journey towards the person's agreed goals, focusing on what is important to them; developed with the person, and their family members or carers (as appropriate); based on advice and input from all members of the multidisciplinary team; written in clear English; a single document or file; shared with the person, their families and carers (as appropriate), the person's GP, and healthcare professionals involved in their ongoing care; re

mcqs.question: When does NICE suggest technology-enabled rehabilitation sessions?

options.A: Only for children and young people
options.C: Never, as only face-to-face is allowed
options.D: When local therapy is hard to access

mcqs.correctAnswerText: When local therapy is hard to access
mcqs.explanation: Technology-enabled sessions can be considered if people want more local, accessible therapy or practitioners are unavailable, for example in rural areas.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider technology-enabled follow-up, support and rehabilitation sessions if people request more local, accessible therapy or if rehabilitation practitioners are not available in their area, for example, in rural areas.

topics.coverageNote: Pool covers ovarian and endometrial cancer. Mostly NICE (ovarian cancer CG122, familial ovarian NG241, TAs from 2005–2024; no sourceYear stored), plus NCCN 2024, ESMO-ESGO 2019, ESGO 2024 and a 2018 SOLO-1 abstract. Guideline-level rows give little endometrial content apart from PMS2 risk reduction.

mcqs.question: Ultrasound, CA125 and clinical findings suggest ovarian cancer. What staging investigation does NICE recommend?
mcqs.explanation: NICE recommends CT of the pelvis and abdomen, adding the thorax if clinically indicated, to establish the extent of disease.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If the ultrasound, serum CA125 and clinical status suggest ovarian cancer, carry out a CT scan of the pelvis and abdomen to establish the extent of the cancer. Include the thorax if clinically indicated.

mcqs.question: What does NICE say about MRI in suspected ovarian cancer?

options.A: Use it to screen the general population

mcqs.explanation: NICE advises against routine MRI for assessing suspected ovarian cancer.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not use MRI routinely for assessing women with suspected ovarian cancer.

mcqs.question: What does NICE state is the surgical objective in ovarian cancer, before or after neoadjuvant chemotherapy?
mcqs.explanation: The objective should be complete resection of all macroscopic disease.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If carrying out surgery for ovarian cancer, whether before chemotherapy or after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, the objective should be complete resection of all macroscopic disease.

mcqs.question: What does NICE say about systematic retroperitoneal lymphadenectomy in apparent stage 1 ovarian cancer?

options.E: Perform it only in young women

mcqs.explanation: NICE says not to include systematic retroperitoneal lymphadenectomy as standard surgery when disease appears confined to the ovaries.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not include systematic retroperitoneal lymphadenectomy (block dissection of lymph nodes from the pelvic side walls to the level of the renal veins) as part of standard surgical treatment in women with suspected ovarian cancer whose cancer appears to be confined to the ovaries (that is, who appear to have stage 1 ovarian cancer).

mcqs.question: A woman has optimally staged grade 1, stage 1a ovarian cancer. What does NICE advise about adjuvant chemotherapy?
mcqs.explanation: NICE advises not offering adjuvant chemotherapy for optimally staged low-risk stage 1 disease (grade 1/2, stage 1a/1b).

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not offer adjuvant chemotherapy to women who have had optimal surgical staging and have low-risk stage 1 ovarian cancer (grade 1 or 2, stage 1a or 1b).

mcqs.question: A patient has grade 3, stage 1c ovarian cancer. What adjuvant treatment does NICE offer?
mcqs.explanation: High-risk stage 1 disease (grade 3 or stage 1c) is offered adjuvant chemotherapy with 6 cycles of carboplatin.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer women with high-risk stage 1 ovarian cancer (grade 3 or stage 1c) adjuvant chemotherapy consisting of 6 cycles of carboplatin.

mcqs.question: When does NICE accept starting chemotherapy for suspected advanced ovarian cancer without a tissue diagnosis?

options.A: Whenever the CT appearance is typical

mcqs.explanation: Chemotherapy without histology or cytology is only offered in exceptional cases, after MDT discussion and a discussion with the woman.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer cytotoxic chemotherapy for suspected advanced ovarian cancer without a tissue diagnosis (histology or cytology) only: in exceptional cases, after discussion with the multidisciplinary team, and after discussing with the woman the possible benefits and risks of starting chemotherapy without a tissue diagnosis.

mcqs.question: What does NICE say about intraperitoneal chemotherapy for ovarian cancer?
mcqs.explanation: NICE says not to offer intraperitoneal chemotherapy except as part of a clinical trial.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not offer intraperitoneal chemotherapy for ovarian cancer, except as part of a clinical trial. See also NICE's HealthTech guidance on cytoreduction surgery with hyperthermic intraoperative peritoneal chemotherapy for peritoneal carcinomatosis , which recommends that this procedure should only be used with special arrangements for clinical governance, consent, and audit or research.

mcqs.question: Which first-line chemotherapy options does NICE technology appraisal TA55 recommend for ovarian cancer?
mcqs.explanation: Paclitaxel with a platinum compound, or platinum-based therapy alone, are options for first-line treatment.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Paclitaxel with a platinum-based compound or with platinum-based therapy alone (cisplatin or carboplatin) are recommended as options for first-line chemotherapy for treating ovarian cancer. For full details, see NICE's technology appraisal guidance on paclitaxel (TA55, 2005) .

mcqs.question: What is olaparib maintenance (TA962) recommended for?
mcqs.explanation: Olaparib maintenance is an option for BRCA mutation-positive stage 3–4 high-grade epithelial ovarian cancer after response to first-line platinum.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Olaparib for maintenance treatment is recommended as an option for BRCA mutation-positive advanced (stage 3 and 4) high-grade epithelial ovarian cancer after response to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy. For full details, see NICE's technology appraisal guidance on olaparib (TA962, 2024) .

mcqs.question: Olaparib plus bevacizumab maintenance is recommended for advanced disease with which molecular feature?
mcqs.explanation: Olaparib with bevacizumab is an option for HRD-positive advanced high-grade disease after response to platinum with bevacizumab.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Olaparib with bevacizumab for maintenance treatment is recommended as an option for homologous recombination deficiency positive, advanced (stage 3 and 4), high-grade epithelial ovarian cancer after complete or partial response to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy with bevacizumab. For full details, see NICE's technology appraisal guidance on olaparib with bevacizumab (TA946, 2024) .

mcqs.question: Under what condition is niraparib maintenance after first-line platinum recommended?

options.A: Only for stage 1 disease after surgery
options.B: If no bevacizumab in first-line induction

mcqs.correctAnswerText: If no bevacizumab in first-line induction
mcqs.explanation: Niraparib maintenance is an option only if the patient didn't have, or couldn't tolerate, bevacizumab in first-line induction.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Niraparib for maintenance treatment is recommended as an option for advanced (stage 3 and 4) high-grade epithelial ovarian cancer in adults after response to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy only if they did not have or could not tolerate bevacizumab as part of first-line induction chemotherapy. For full details, see NICE's technology appraisal guidance on niraparib (TA1129, 2026) .

mcqs.question: What does NICE advise about aspirin and ovarian cancer risk?

options.A: Offer it to all women over 50
options.B: Don't offer it solely for that
options.D: Offer daily aspirin to all carriers
options.E: Offer it together with the pill

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Don't offer it solely for that
mcqs.explanation: NICE says not to offer aspirin for the sole purpose of reducing ovarian cancer risk.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not offer aspirin for the sole purpose of reducing ovarian cancer risk.

mcqs.question: If a familial ovarian cancer MDT carries out surveillance, which CA125 strategy does NICE describe?
mcqs.explanation: Surveillance uses serial 4-monthly CA125 testing with an algorithm of demonstrated accuracy, such as ROCA.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If carrying out surveillance (see recommendation 1.8.19), the familial ovarian cancer multidisciplinary team should: carry out serial 4‑monthly CA125 longitudinal testing using an algorithm with demonstrated accuracy (for example, the Risk of Ovarian Cancer Algorithm [ROCA] Test); coordinate, audit and interpret CA125 testing using a call and recall system; have a review appointment with the person at least once a year to discuss the recommendation of having risk-reducing surgery (see the sectio

mcqs.question: What should people choosing surveillance instead of risk-reducing surgery be told?

options.C: It isn't an alternative to surgery
options.E: Surveillance is proven to save lives

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It isn't an alternative to surgery
mcqs.explanation: Surveillance may detect cancer earlier, but there is little evidence it improves outcomes or saves lives, so it isn't an alternative to surgery.

sourceRefs.excerpt: although regular surveillance means that ovarian cancer may be detected earlier, they should not view surveillance as an alternative to risk-reducing surgery (because there is little evidence on whether this leads to improved outcomes and saves lives)

mcqs.question: A 46-year-old has a heterozygous PMS2 variant and no family history of ovarian cancer. What does NICE suggest considering?
mcqs.explanation: NICE suggests considering hysterectomy alone (no earlier than 45) to prevent endometrial cancer in PMS2 heterozygotes without an ovarian family history.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider risk-reducing total hysterectomy alone to prevent endometrial cancer for people (no earlier than 45 years) who have: a heterozygous PMS2 pathogenic variant and no family history of ovarian cancer.

mcqs.question: A BRCA1 carrier considering oophorectomy before 40 asks about the pill. What does NICE (2004) advise?

options.A: Prescribe it to all BRCA1 carriers
options.B: Not purely to reduce ovarian risk
options.C: Prescribe it to protect the breasts

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Not purely to reduce ovarian risk
mcqs.explanation: The oral contraceptive pill shouldn't be prescribed purely to reduce ovarian cancer risk in this group.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If a woman has a BRCA1 mutation and is considering a risk-reducing oophorectomy before the age of 40 years, the oral contraceptive pill should not be prescribed purely for the reduction in ovarian cancer risk. [2004]

mcqs.question: What is NICE's TA284 position on adding bevacizumab to paclitaxel and carboplatin first-line?
mcqs.explanation: TA284 doesn't recommend it, although NHS England recommends it as a first-line option.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Bevacizumab with paclitaxel and carboplatin is not recommended for the first-line treatment of advanced ovarian cancer. For full details, see NICE's technology appraisal guidance on bevacizumab (TA284, 2013) . However, NHS England recommends bevacizumab with paclitaxel and carboplatin as an option for first-line induction treatment for advanced (stage 3 and 4) ovarian cancer at a dose of 7.5 mg/kg or 15 mg/kg. For more information, see the NHS England Cancer Drugs Fund list . In April 2025, a do

mcqs.question: Who should run the familial ovarian cancer MDT and which expertise should it include, according to NICE?

options.C: Breast surgeons only, with no geneticist
options.D: Primary care team with no named lead

mcqs.explanation: The MDT should have a designated lead clinician and include expertise in clinical genetics, gynaecology and gynaecological oncology.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The familial ovarian cancer multidisciplinary team should have a designated lead clinician, and include healthcare professionals with expertise in areas including: clinical genetics; gynaecology; gynaecological oncology.

mcqs.question: Asymptomatic cancer is found on histology after risk-reducing surgery. What does NICE advise?

options.E: Refer to the gynaecology oncology MDT

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Refer to the gynaecology oncology MDT
mcqs.explanation: Refer the person to the gynaecology oncology multidisciplinary team.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If asymptomatic cancer is identified by preoperative investigation or postoperative histopathological or cytopathological analysis, refer the person to the gynaecology oncology multidisciplinary team (see the section on the gynaecology oncology multidisciplinary team ).

topics.coverageNote: All rows are NICE psychosis/schizophrenia recommendations for adults (CG178) and children (CG155), with 2009–2019 tags and no stored sourceYear, so the topic can't be dated. No trial rows.

mcqs.question: Schizophrenia hasn't responded to adequate sequential doses of two antipsychotics, one a non-clozapine SGA. What does NICE offer?
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers clozapine after an inadequate response to at least 2 antipsychotics, at least 1 being a non-clozapine second-generation drug.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer clozapine to people with schizophrenia whose illness has not responded adequately to treatment despite the sequential use of adequate doses of at least 2 different antipsychotic drugs. At least 1 of the drugs should be a non-clozapine second-generation antipsychotic. [2009]

mcqs.question: For children and young people, how long should each of the two antipsychotics be tried before NICE offers clozapine?
mcqs.explanation: In children and young people, each of the two antipsychotics should be used for 6–8 weeks before clozapine.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer clozapine to children and young people with schizophrenia whose illness has not responded adequately to pharmacological treatment despite the sequential use of adequate doses of at least two different antipsychotic drugs each used for 6 to 8 weeks. [2013]

mcqs.question: The response to optimised clozapine is inadequate. What does NICE say about adding a second antipsychotic?

options.B: Check levels; trial may need 8–10 wks
options.D: Add one immediately for a week
options.E: Pick a drug with the same side effects

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Check levels; trial may need 8–10 wks
mcqs.explanation: Measure therapeutic drug levels before augmenting. An adequate augmentation trial may need 8–10 weeks.

sourceRefs.excerpt: For people with schizophrenia whose illness has not responded adequately to clozapine at an optimised dose, healthcare professionals should consider recommendation 1.5.7.1 (including measuring therapeutic drug levels) before adding a second antipsychotic to augment treatment with clozapine. An adequate trial of such an augmentation may need to be up to 8 to 10 weeks. Choose a drug that does not compound the common side effects of clozapine. [2009]

mcqs.question: When does NICE suggest considering a depot or long-acting injectable antipsychotic?

options.B: Only when care is managed in primary care
options.C: Only in children and young people

mcqs.explanation: Depots are considered when the person prefers them after an acute episode, or when avoiding covert non-adherence is a clinical priority.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider offering depot/long-acting injectable antipsychotic medication to people with psychosis or schizophrenia: who would prefer such treatment after an acute episode; where avoiding covert non-adherence (either intentional or unintentional) to antipsychotic medication is a clinical priority within the treatment plan. [2009]

mcqs.question: What does NICE say about antipsychotics for symptoms that don't meet a psychosis diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: NICE says not to offer antipsychotics for sub-threshold symptoms or to reduce the risk of psychosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not offer antipsychotic medication: for psychotic symptoms or mental state changes that are not sufficient for a diagnosis of psychosis or schizophrenia, or with the aim of decreasing the risk of psychosis. [2013]

mcqs.question: What does NICE recommend for an acute exacerbation of schizophrenia in an adult?

options.C: Antipsychotic with family therapy and CBT

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Antipsychotic with family therapy and CBT
mcqs.explanation: NICE offers oral antipsychotics together with psychological interventions (family intervention and individual CBT).

sourceRefs.excerpt: For people with an acute exacerbation or recurrence of psychosis or schizophrenia, offer: oral antipsychotic medication (see the section on how to use antipsychotic medication ) in conjunction with; psychological interventions (family intervention and individual CBT, delivered as described in the section on how to deliver psychological interventions ). [2014]

mcqs.question: What does NICE advise about starting antipsychotics for a first presentation of sustained psychosis in primary care?

options.A: Never start any medication at all
options.C: Start freely and review in 6 weeks
options.D: Start two drugs to speed the response
options.E: Start a depot to ensure adherence

mcqs.explanation: Antipsychotics shouldn't be started in primary care for a first presentation unless done in consultation with a consultant psychiatrist.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not start antipsychotic medication for a first presentation of sustained psychotic symptoms in primary care unless it is done in consultation with a consultant psychiatrist. [2009, amended 2014]

mcqs.question: When does NICE accept regular combined antipsychotic medication?

options.D: Only for short periods, e.g. when switching
options.E: For treatment resistance instead of clozapine

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Only for short periods, e.g. when switching
mcqs.explanation: NICE advises against starting regular combined antipsychotics except for short periods such as when changing medication.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not initiate regular combined antipsychotic medication, except for short periods (for example, when changing medication). [2009]

mcqs.question: What does NICE say about a loading dose ('rapid neuroleptisation')?

options.B: Use it for all acute admissions

mcqs.explanation: NICE says not to use a loading dose of antipsychotic.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not use a loading dose of antipsychotic medication (often referred to as 'rapid neuroleptisation'). [2009]

mcqs.question: A person with schizophrenia who takes clozapine wants to stop smoking. What does NICE highlight?

options.A: Only nicotine patches are unsafe here

mcqs.explanation: Offer smoking cessation help, but be aware that cutting down can significantly affect metabolism of clozapine and olanzapine.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer people with psychosis or schizophrenia who smoke help to stop smoking, even if previous attempts have been unsuccessful. Be aware of the potential significant impact of reducing cigarette smoking on the metabolism of other drugs, particularly clozapine and olanzapine. [2014]

mcqs.question: When does NICE say an ECG should be offered before starting antipsychotics?

options.E: Only in children and young people

mcqs.explanation: An ECG is offered if the SPC specifies it, there is CV risk on examination, a personal CV history, or the person is being admitted.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Before starting antipsychotic medication, offer the person with psychosis or schizophrenia an electrocardiogram (ECG) if: specified in the summary of product characteristics (SPC); a physical examination has identified specific cardiovascular risk (such as diagnosis of high blood pressure); there is a personal history of cardiovascular disease or the service user is being admitted as an inpatient. [2009]

mcqs.question: Which psychological intervention does NICE advise against routinely offering as a specific intervention?
mcqs.explanation: NICE advises against routinely offering counselling and supportive psychotherapy, although preferences should be considered.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not routinely offer counselling and supportive psychotherapy (as specific interventions) to people with psychosis or schizophrenia. However, take service user preferences into account, especially if other more efficacious psychological treatments, such as CBT, family intervention and arts therapies, are not available locally. [2009]

mcqs.question: What does NICE suggest for alleviating negative symptoms?
mcqs.explanation: NICE suggests considering arts therapies for all people with psychosis, particularly for negative symptoms.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider offering arts therapies to all people with psychosis or schizophrenia, particularly for the alleviation of negative symptoms. This can be started either during the acute phase or later, including in inpatient settings. [2009]

mcqs.question: Who should be offered family intervention, according to NICE?

options.A: Families living with or close to the person
options.B: Only after three or more relapses
options.C: Only if individual CBT has failed
options.D: Only families of children and young people

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Families living with or close to the person
mcqs.explanation: Offer family intervention to all families who live with or are in close contact with the service user.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer family intervention to all families of people with psychosis or schizophrenia who live with or are in close contact with the service user (delivered as described in recommendation 1.3.7.2 ). This can be started either during the acute phase or later, including in inpatient settings. [2009]

mcqs.question: What does NICE say about adherence therapy as a specific intervention for children and young people with psychosis?
mcqs.explanation: NICE says not to offer adherence therapy as a specific intervention to children and young people with psychosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not offer adherence therapy (as a specific intervention) to children and young people with psychosis or schizophrenia. [2013]

mcqs.question: What does NICE offer people with psychosis, especially those on antipsychotics, to support physical health?
mcqs.explanation: Mental healthcare providers should offer a combined healthy eating and physical activity programme (unchanged after the 2019 STEPWISE review).

sourceRefs.excerpt: People with psychosis or schizophrenia, especially those taking antipsychotics, should be offered a combined healthy eating and physical activity programme by their mental healthcare provider. Our 2019 review of the STEPWISE trial did not change this recommendation. [2019]

mcqs.question: When does NICE suggest intensive case management?
mcqs.explanation: Consider intensive case management for people likely to disengage from treatment or services.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider intensive case management for people with psychosis or schizophrenia who are likely to disengage from treatment or services. [2014]

mcqs.question: When does NICE suggest extending early intervention in psychosis services beyond 3 years?
mcqs.explanation: Consider extending EIP beyond 3 years if there hasn't been a stable recovery.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider extending the availability of early intervention in psychosis services beyond 3 years if the person has not made a stable recovery from psychosis or schizophrenia. [2014]

mcqs.question: Which antipsychotic is a NICE TA option for 15–17-year-olds with schizophrenia when risperidone is contraindicated?
mcqs.explanation: TA213 recommends aripiprazole for 15–17-year-olds in whom risperidone is contraindicated.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Aripiprazole is recommended as an option in NICE technology appraisal guidance for treating schizophrenia in people aged 15 to 17 years for whom risperidone is contraindicated. For full details, see the guidance on aripiprazole (TA213, 2011) .

mcqs.question: An acute episode in the community exceeds the capacity of early intervention services. What does NICE offer first-line?

options.A: Primary care follow-up within a week
options.C: Peer support alone in the community

mcqs.explanation: Crisis resolution and home treatment teams are first-line during an acute community episode when severity or risk exceeds EIP or community team capacity.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer crisis resolution and home treatment teams as a first-line service to support people with psychosis or schizophrenia during an acute episode in the community if the severity of the episode, or the level of risk to self or others, exceeds the capacity of the early intervention in psychosis services or other community teams to effectively manage it. [2014]
